title: ClaimScene — narrated demo walkthrough
description: Per-beat, audio-locked script. build_video.py synthesizes each narration line (ElevenLabs), locks the beat's visual duration to the measured audio, and renders a gentle Ken Burns move across the committed forensic-blueprint cards in demo/assets/. check_video.py re-verifies the rendered mp4 against this file.

beats.caption: Honest accident documentation. Illustrated, never faked.
beats.narration: After a crash, the first real job is documentation. Which cars, which damage, which road, and what actually happened. ClaimScene turns accident photos into a case a claims handler can trust. Honest, illustrated, and never faked.

beats.caption: A convincing AI guess is dangerous as evidence.
beats.narration: That matters now, because generative video made accident scenes easy to fake and hard to trust. A convincing AI reconstruction that is really just a guess is dangerous as evidence. Insurers and courts are already warning about synthetic media in claims.

beats.caption: Two layers. The app never lets them blur.
beats.narration: So ClaimScene splits every case into two layers, and it never lets them blur.

beats.caption: Constrained scene, then a deterministic schematic.
beats.narration: The photos become a constrained scene the model cannot invent coordinates in. It may only fill a closed vocabulary of enums, clock positions, and speed bands. Deterministic code turns that into a top-down schematic, the factual layer, where the same input always produces the same bytes.

beats.caption: A disclosed AI illustration, sealed on Backblaze B2.
beats.narration: Beside it sits a clearly disclosed AI illustration, watermarked, and never merged with the facts. Both layers, and every input photo, are sealed on Backblaze B2 with each photo's source and license recorded.

beats.caption: AI proposes. You confirm.
beats.narration: The middle step is the whole point. The AI only proposes the scene. You review and adjust it with constrained dropdowns and a twelve-position clock, never free-text coordinates, and the schematic redraws live as you edit. AI proposes, you confirm. Nothing is sealed until you render.

beats.caption: Manifest proves AI vs human. Verify runs 14 checks.
beats.narration: Here is the difference. The sealed manifest proves what the AI proposed against what the human corrected, such as changing vehicle A's colour. Press Verify, and the SHA-256 seal recomputes right in your browser, backed by a receipt of fourteen named checks over the stored bytes.

beats.caption: 100% weighted field accuracy, on the record.
beats.narration: And the accuracy is measured, not asserted. The primary model scores one hundred percent weighted field accuracy on a committed seven-scenario evaluation set, with a dated scoreboard living in the repo.

beats.caption: gemma / gemini · Genblaze · Backblaze B2 · Cloud Run.
beats.narration: Under the hood: a Gemma and Gemini vision ladder, Genblaze for the seedream still and pixverse clip, Backblaze B2 storage, and Cloud Run. Live where credentials exist, deterministic fakes everywhere else, so the whole pipeline runs offline in continuous integration.

beats.caption: Live on Cloud Run. Open source.
beats.narration: ClaimScene is live on Cloud Run, and the whole project is open source. Honest accident documentation. Illustrated, and never faked.
